# Tokyo Family Stay Plan: Apr 10–14, 2026

A practical family booking plan for **2 adults + 2 children (8, 11)** with a total target of **¥180,000** for lodging and dinner reservations. I’m assuming a **mid-range 3–4 star hotel**, one family room or two connected rooms if needed, and **kid-friendly dinners** near major train lines.

## Recommended Booking Mix

| Item | Target | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hotel stay | **¥130,000–¥155,000** | 4 nights, non-smoking, breakfast included, near a station |
| Dinner reservations | **¥20,000–¥40,000** | 3–4 dinners, family-friendly casual or set-menu spots |
| Buffer | **¥5,000–¥15,000** | Taxes, service fees, drinks, or room upgrades |

## Mid-Range Hotel Shortlist

Option 1: **Shinagawa / Tokyo Station area hotel** | Best for easy rail access and airport connections | Near major JR lines and family-friendly transit
Action: [Button: Check rates](https://www.booking.com/city/jp/tokyo.html)

Option 2: **Ueno / Asakusa area hotel** | Good value, easy subway access, more budget-friendly dining nearby | Often strong breakfast-included options
Action: [Button: Check rates](https://www.agoda.com/city/tokyo-jp.html)

Option 3: **Shinjuku / Ikebukuro area hotel** | Strong transport links and lots of dining choices | Good if you want convenience over quiet
Action: [Button: Check rates](https://www.expedia.com/Tokyo-Hotels.d179900.Travel-Guide-Hotels)

## Day-by-Day Booking Outline

### Day 1: Fri, Apr 10 — Arrival and easy dinner
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- **Hotel:** Check in to a non-smoking family room near a station.
- **Dinner:** Book a simple first-night reservation within 10–15 minutes of the hotel.
- **Best choice:** Casual Japanese set meals, ramen, curry, or a family diner with seat reservations.

### Day 2: Sat, Apr 11 — Central Tokyo dinner
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/train-front.svg
- **Hotel:** Keep the same base for easy movement.
- **Dinner:** Reserve an early table near a major hub like Tokyo, Shibuya, or Ueno.
- **Best choice:** Family-friendly izakaya with private booth, teishoku restaurant, or sushi chain with reservations.

### Day 3: Sun, Apr 12 — Flexible sightseeing day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/map.svg
- **Hotel:** Confirm breakfast times and luggage storage.
- **Dinner:** Choose a neighborhood spot near your sightseeing area to reduce transit time.
- **Best choice:** Tempura, tonkatsu, udon, or a casual grill restaurant that accepts children.

### Day 4: Mon, Apr 13 — Final full day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar.svg
- **Hotel:** Reconfirm late check-out if needed.
- **Dinner:** Book a relaxed final dinner near the hotel or station.
- **Best choice:** Set-course meal under budget, or a buffet with child pricing.

### Day 5: Tue, Apr 14 — Checkout and departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg
- **Hotel:** Early breakfast, checkout, and luggage forwarding if needed.
- **Dinner:** No dinner reservation needed unless your departure is late.
- **Best choice:** Keep this day open for travel and airport transfer.

## Reservation Details to Prepare

### Hotel booking details
- Full names for all 4 guests exactly as on passports
- Child ages: **8** and **11**
- Room preference: **non-smoking**
- Bed setup: **1 family room** or **2 beds + extra bedding**
- Breakfast: **included**
- Station preference: within **5–10 minutes walk**
- Arrival time and flight number
- Any need for crib, extra pillows, or adjoining rooms
- Payment card that supports international hotel pre-authorization

### Dinner reservation details
- Number of guests: **4**
- Two children ages **8** and **11**
- Preferred time: usually **5:30–7:00 PM** for family convenience
- Seating preference: booth, table, or private room if available
- Dietary notes: allergies, no raw fish, vegetarian needs, or spice limits
- Budget target per dinner: helpful to mention if booking by phone or form
- Contact phone or email for confirmations
- Backup plan if the restaurant does not accept children

## Budget-Friendly Booking Strategy

- Put **most of the budget into the hotel**, because breakfast-included and station-adjacent properties tend to save time and transit cost.
- Keep dinners to **2–4 reservations max**; leave some evenings open for casual meals.
- Prefer hotels near **JR Yamanote**, **Tokyo Metro**, or a major interchange to reduce taxi use.
- Book hotel first, then dinner reservations once your sightseeing areas are set.

## Quick Actions
